verificationMethod: Pricing is verified daily against vendor sources. Small drift (under 25% on input and output) is auto-applied; larger changes are reviewed by a human editor before publication. Vendor pricing pages are the canonical source of truth.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.notes: Best-in-class reasoning. Anthropic's flagship for the hardest agentic decisions.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.notes: The sweet spot. Handles ~90% of agent workflows at a fraction of Opus pricing.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.notes: Fast and cheap. Best for high-volume classification and short replies.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.notes: OpenAI's frontier line. Marketed for coding and professional work.

models.name: Grok 4.20
models.notes: xAI's current flagship. 2M context with live web access via X integration.

models.name: Grok 4
models.notes: xAI's previous flagship. Still available; most builders should default to Grok 4.20.

models.name: Grok 4 Fast
models.notes: xAI's value tier. 10× cheaper than Grok 4.20 with the same 2M context.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.notes: Largest context window on the list. Pricing shown is for prompts ≤200k tokens; rises to $2.50/$15 above that.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.notes: Hybrid reasoning model with 1M context and tunable thinking budgets.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Preview
models.notes: Google's most cost-efficient model. Optimised for high-volume agentic tasks and simple data processing.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B (Together AI)
models.notes: Open weights. The price shown reflects Together AI; other inference providers host the same weights at different rates.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.notes: DeepSeek's value tier. Cache-hit pricing drops input to $0.0028/M on repeat queries.

models.name: Kimi K2
models.notes: Moonshot AI's frontier model. Strong on long-context work.

models.name: GLM-4.6
models.notes: Formerly Zhipu AI. Competitive Chinese frontier model with strong coding and tool-use benchmarks.

models.name: Mistral Large 2.1
models.notes: European frontier model. Stronger data residency story than US providers — useful for EU compliance-heavy workflows.
